_readme: Controller-owned. Only the gatekeeper (VS Code Claude session) writes verified fields, after observing the target environment directly (az containerapp show / live smoke probes) -- never from reading source, a merged PR, or an agent's claim. External agents may read this file and may propose an update in a PR, but the PR does not become truth until the gatekeeper re-observes and re-writes it. Use null / 'not_verified' rather than guessing; a wrong value here is worse than an honest gap.

The revision idles at ScaledToZero and was woken by an HTTPS GET (200) during this observation, after which az reported Running -- scale-to-zero is normal for staging, not an outage. That digest is byte-identical to the release digest deploy-staging run 31854517806 (head_sha 187f406b) printed as its last line, and the same run's SHADOW E2E gate log reads 'SHADOW INTAKE GATE PASS' (read from the log, not the step conclusion). Staging sets no PPBF_RELEASE_SHA env; commit identity binds through the digest chain. BEYOND IDENTITY, this deployment carries authenticated runtime proof: on 2026-08-15 a 41-probe suite ran against this exact revision with sessions minted for the pre-existing gate fixture accounts (gate-session.mjs, all revoked after) -- 41 PASS, 0 FAIL, 5 NOT_VERIFIED (browser-rendered failure states, athlete_voice exclusion, magic-link issuance). Proven live: session-script delivery end to end (one-live-per-coach, restore-on-reload, target-block navigation incl. foreign-block 422, server-owned pause/resume clock frozen-then-advancing, explicit completed AND abandoned settlement, settled immutability, honest history incl. null-not-zero), coach review read-back with attribution and unassigned-coach refusal, coverage grant/revoke with org and active-coach refusals, escalation file->coach-sees->acknowledge->coach-resolve-refused->admin-resolve with cross-coach invisibility, activation-codes owner-403/admin-200, guardian messages read, and deployed-bundle copy checks (BREAK MY 40% RULE absent; credential-policy invite copy present). Probe fixtures remain in the staging database, all named zzprobe/ZZ RUNTIME PROBE.
known_staging_gaps: Outbound mail RESOLVED 2026-08-08T18:07Z. It was never a permissions gap and never a code gap: a token probe inside the container showed roles=["Mail.Send"], and the refusal carried graph_error_code=ErrorAccessDenied, which is Exchange's application access policy rather than Entra. The policy was created 07:13Z and began enforcing between 07:54Z (last refusal) and 18:07Z (first success). Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy reported Granted the whole time because it evaluates configured state, not enforced state -- worth remembering before trusting it again.

Under the gate's two-consecutive threshold, so no run failed. The 2026-08-15 gate run (31854517806) passed; its per-step retry behaviour was not re-inspected, so this history is carried, not extended.

Session-script reference seed remains blocked: two of its 65 blocks violate pilot_ssb_content (block_kind='instruction' with no what_to_* content), the load is atomic so 0 of 65 apply, and the loader is deliberately excluded from seed-reference-data.yml. Reproduced by dry-run against staging 2026-08-15. Staging's only session scripts are the zzprobe fixtures; fix belongs to the seed DATA, not this file.

known_production_gaps: Production reference data is NOT seeded -- re-observed directly 2026-08-15: pilot.drill_library and pilot.disciplines both count 0 rows. The schema is present and the code is deployed, but seed-reference-data has never been run against production, so /coach/cohorts and /coach/disciplines render empty lists -- missing data, not a broken page. Still blocked on seed_account_id: drill-library (and therefore dataset 'all') requires it, production's active platform owner is Admin@punxsyprominence.org with a CAPITAL A, the lowercase row is retired, and no read-only workflow exposes the id -- it has to come from a human who can read it out of the database. Production also has ZERO session scripts (the seed for those is separately blocked on pilot_ssb_content, see the staging entry), so the newly deployed /coach/session-scripts browse renders an honest empty state until either seed is fixed or scripts are authored.

Magic-link mail delivery is not_verified on production. It has never been attempted here -- no production account has auth_provider='magic_link', so nothing would be sent. Staging's refusal has since resolved on its own (see the staging entry), so the tenant-level condition that caused it is gone; production still needs its own access policy checked before anything is claimed.

T-001 and T-002 reached production without a RUNTIME_VERIFIED row and still have none. Their PRs (#239, #242) merged 2026-08-06 and rode to production inside a deploy of main dispatched for the magic-link work. The pipeline's own rule is that no item may skip a state; two still have. T-003 was in this list and came out of it the honest way -- its probe was actually run on 2026-08-08 (see capabilities.runtime_verified), not backfilled.

Read from the run log, NOT from the database: 60 of the list's migrations were counted PASS directly and the remainder are covered by the step's own success (the loop exits non-zero on any failure), so this is an observation of the runner, not of the schema. SIGNIFICANCE BEYOND THE SCHEMA BEING CURRENT: this is the first migration=all to succeed on production since run 69 (2026-08-08T16:59Z), and the first since the drills readiness contradiction was fixed. Between those two runs the production migration path was BROKEN AND UNAWARE OF IT -- run 69 installed drill-versioning, which replaces pilot_drills_one_name_per_org with a partial unique index, while pilot-apply-drills still required a total one and runs earlier in the list. Nothing surfaced because nobody re-dispatched production in that window; staging runs 70/71/72 died on it. What changed tonight is not that the schema advanced (it was already current) but that the path is repeatable.

schema.note: This is a log of what has been OBSERVED applied via apply-migrations run output, not a generated schema version. Every pilot:apply-* runner is additive/idempotent, so re-running one is safe -- this list exists to avoid re-running unnecessarily, not to gate anything. Added 2026-08-10: entries here record what a RUNNER reported, which is weaker than reading the schema back. A green apply-migrations run proves each runner's own readiness assertion passed -- and the drills incident showed a readiness assertion can itself be wrong, so a gatekeeper checking a specific object should still query for it rather than trust this list.

runtime_verified: magic-link redemption on staging: POST /api/pilot/auth/magic-link/consume returns 200 and sets ppbf_pilot_session for the correct principal; the same token replayed returns TOKEN_ALREADY_USED; GET returns 405 with Allow: POST so a mail scanner's prefetch cannot burn a link; exactly one session row created (2026-08-08, staging)

magic-link DELIVERY on staging, the whole chain with a human in it (2026-08-08T18:07-18:12Z): request answered 202 and wrote a token row; no magic_link.issue_failed line on a warm container; the mail arrived in a real mailbox; the owner clicked it; consumed_at 18:12:51.064Z. Silence alone would not have proved this -- issueMagicLink is deliberately silent for an unknown address too -- so the token row was read back to separate 'sent' from 'no such account'.

magic-link single-transaction claim: the session row's created_at is 18:12:51.064Z, identical to the token's consumed_at, confirming the claim and the session insert happen in one transaction rather than two writes that could interleave. Exactly one session for that account from that click, and the only other session in the window belongs to a Microsoft sign-in by the owner.

magic-link supersession: every older token row carries invalidated_at set by the request that followed it, and no two were ever live at once -- so requesting a second link genuinely kills the first rather than leaving both valid.

T-003 quarantined-video scan-review console (2026-08-08, retroactive). Acceptance criteria: page.test.tsx 5/5 including a WrongRoleNotice case for a non-deciding role and separate approve and block cases. Role gate proven against the DEPLOYED app, not only against mocks: a real coach session returns 403 'Forbidden: role not allowed' on POST /api/pilot/video/scan-review, which is the ticket's P0 rule (the coach who filmed footage of a minor gets no path into the decision). A real platform_owner session is refused identically -- VIDEO_REVIEW_DECIDE_ROLES is ['organization_admin'] and nothing else, so even the platform owner cannot decide. Unauthenticated, video/list, review-link and scan-review all answer 401 on BOTH environments and /admin/video-review renders 200. Production has 4 active organization_admin accounts, so the console is usable by someone. Probe sessions were minted on staging only and deleted in a finally block; 0 remained. No session was minted on production and no real video was approved or blocked anywhere.
